topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and progression models
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and framing how genetic mutations drive the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in signaling cascades such as Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta drive cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to exit the cell cycle and differentiate properly in hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of evasion of apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how p53 inactivation and the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere maintenance, TERT reactivation, and p53 stress-response pathways regulate cellular lifespan and immortalization before reviewing these growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the shift toward aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring across tumor types, and how metabolic enzyme mutations produce oncometabolites that alter gene expression.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the requirement and mechanisms for new blood vessel formation to supply growing tumors with oxygen and nutrients.

topics.label: Tumor dissemination, metastasis, and clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms, anatomical routes, inefficiency, and genomic features associated with cancer invasion and metastatic spread.

topics.label: Lecture summary and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing the universality of cancer hallmarks, recommending further reading, and taking final questions.
